questions.problem:
Find the volume of the solid $R$ given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,1\le y\le 4,\,2\le z\le 3y+x\}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that we have a three-dimensional type I region.

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{2}^{3y+x}\,dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{4}[z]_{z=2}^{z=3y+x}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{4}3y+x-2\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2}+xy-2y]}_{y=1}^{y=4}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\,[(24+4x-8)-(\frac{3}{2}+x-2)]\,dx \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{2}3x+\frac{33}{2}\,dx \\  & ={[\frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{33}{2}x]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =\frac{3(2)^{2}}{2}+\frac{33}{2}(2)-0 \\  & =39.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the volume of the solid region above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the top one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14209435/assets/0ba756dacf72b89b06c3c214e1582a74fa803f567082f57538e7a78c84d4591f.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type I region

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,0\le z\le 2+x-y\},
$$

where

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 1\}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14209435/assets/65c61ad7dc2964cd0de9a6bbdf259fcf3388e25da4eaabf155d58ff0c05c8d55.png)

Hence, the type I representation of $R$ is

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 2+x-y\}
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2+x-y}dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}[z]_{z=0}^{z=2+x-y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2+x-y)-0\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}2+x-y\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[(2+x)y-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2+x-\frac{1}{2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{3}{2}+x\,dx \\  & ={[\frac{3}{2}x+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =(3+2)-0 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that our solid can be written as the type I region

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,0\le z\le 3+x-y\},
$$

where

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 2\}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14209435/assets/74954715928551ebb271cdfd461d783778b02b7944cbfd5502d6d06011408ad8.png)

Hence, the type I representation of $R$ is

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 3+x-y\}
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3+x-y}dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}[z]_{z=0}^{z=3+x-y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(3+x-y)-0\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}3+x-y\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[(3+x)y-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}((3+x)(2)-\frac{{2}^{2}}{2})-0\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}4+2x\,dx \\  & =[4x+{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =(8+4)-0 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$
